done_when: A thread follow-up starts a turn only when the new batch has a message from an allowed sender, proven by a test where only the root sender is allowed and another person's follow-up gets no reply

findings.body: The new test cannot finish with a real database: `settled()` waits for `last_agent_timestamp`, but production no longer writes that cursor. The migration at apps/core/src/adapters/storage/postgres/schema/migrations/20261001084406_delete_last_agent_timestamp.sql:1 deletes it, while message consumption now updates `consumedAt` and `consumedBy` (apps/core/src/adapters/storage/postgres/repositories/live-admission-work-item-repository.postgres.ts:198). Consequently, the first Bob follow-up wait times out before the remaining authorization assertions execute. Observe the real input-consumption state instead. This is new evidence of a broken test, rather than a renewed request for end-to-end coverage for a small fix.
findings.title: Not done: answers a thread follow-up only when its sender may trigger the agent (real runner)

findings.body: The added line brings this file to 701 lines against the enforced 700-line budget in scripts/architecture-map.json:17. The supplied close run confirms that `check:architecture` fails here and stops the command before typechecking and tests. This violates “each commit leaves the build working”; docs/review-instructions.md:6–8 also explicitly makes new architecture violations blocking and forbids waiving file-size violations. Make a substantive code reduction so the required check passes.
findings.title: Standard: each commit leaves the build working

why: Anyone can get a reply in a thread an allowed person started, because the thread check never looks at who sent the new message
